messages:
From: Samuel Park <sam.park@medivari.com>

Cc: MediVari Legal <legalops@medivari.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood order form + security exhibit — a couple open asks

Ben — thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Legal had a quick pass on the MSA + Order Form and flagged the security exhibit and audit rights sections. Two quick asks before we can route this to procurement: (1) confirmation on SOC 2 report cadence and whether Redwood will accept a bridge letter between annual reports; (2) pen test timing & whether Redwood will commit to a pre-notice window and scoped environment for external testing.

I've attached the redline they annotated (see referenced attachments) and included the high-level concerns inline below. Procurement also asked for a sample evidence cadence showing how SOC2 artifacts and pen-test reports would be handed off during onboarding.

High-level asks from MediVari legal:
- SOC 2 Attestation: annual report + SOC2 Type II acceptable; need clarity on whether a bridge letter is sufficient if timing doesn't align with signing.
- Pen Test: want a 14-day notice window for scheduling and a defined scope that excludes customer data and production user traffic; request for a copy of Redwood's pen-test plan.
- Audit Rights: prefer a bounded on-site inspection option once per 12 months; also want SLA on turnaround for evidence requests (48–72 hours typical).

Can you route this to your security/legal folks and come back with proposed contract language or a one-page runbook for evidence handoff? We want to avoid redline cycles if possible.

Thanks — Sam
Samuel Park
Director, IT Risk — MediVari Health

Subject: Re: Redwood order form + security exhibit — proposed redline language and evidence runbook

Team — drafted focused language to reduce back-and-forth. Below are three short insertions (MSA Exhibit / Order Form) and a one-page evidence cadence summary. I kept the commitments narrow and operational so we don't create an open-ended inspection obligation.

Proposed MSA Exhibit snippets (for discussion):
1) SOC 2: "Customer may request Provider's most recent SOC 2 Type II attestation report. In the event Provider's most recent attestation predates the Effective Date, Provider may deliver a qualified bridge letter from its independent auditor covering the gap until the next attestation is available."

2) Penetration Testing: "Penetration testing of Provider systems may be conducted by either party's third-party testing firm only by mutual agreement and in accordance with Provider's pen-testing engagement playbook. Provider will provide a non-production or scoped testing environment where feasible; where testing against production is unavoidable, Provider will require a 14-calendar-day scheduling notice and will coordinate timing to avoid peak traffic. Provider will not authorize testing that targets customer PII or attempts to exfiltrate production user data."

3) Audit Rights / Evidence: "Customer may request evidence reasonably necessary to validate Provider's compliance with the Security Exhibit. Provider will acknowledge evidence requests within 48 hours and will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide requested artifacts within the timeframes specified in the evidence cadence table attached to the Order Form; for urgent requests tied to active incidents, Provider will prioritize disclosure subject to applicable law and third-party data limitations."

One-page evidence cadence (summary to include as Order Form appendix):
- SOC2 report & bridge letter: delivery upon request (PDF), typical turnaround 24–48 hours from release location;
- Pen-test high-level summary and remediation statement: within 10 business days of completion;
- Specific artifact requests (logs, configs): initial acknowledgement 48 hours; targeted delivery windows: host-level logs (7 business days), aggregated telemetry (10 business days), backup snapshots (not provided without court order).

Karthik: please review the pen-test paragraph — I avoided providing specific tooling or internal runbook details, but we should confirm wording re: scoped testing vs. production. Vanessa: flag any legal escalation language we should include for on-site samples vs. remote, and whether we want to add a cap on inspection frequency (I propose once per 12 months, remote-first).

Happy to send this to Sam as redline-friendly text if team signs off.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett | Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Samuel Park <sam.park@medivari.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: MediVari Legal <legalops@medivari.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood order form + security exhibit — proposed redline language and evidence runbook

Ben/Laura — thank you, this is very helpful and much more prescriptive than the initial draft. A few quick confirmations from our side: (1) bridge letter language is acceptable in principle, we will confirm with procurement that a bridge letter + SOC2 PDF meets their control requirement; (2) the 14-calendar-day notice for production testing is OK provided there is an agreed escalation path if a critical vulnerability is discovered during security assessment; (3) the 48-hour acknowledgement for evidence requests meets our need.

Next steps: MediVari legal will convert Laura's snippets into their markup and push a single PDF to the HubSpot deal. If Redwood can accept the inspection frequency cap of once per 12 months (remote-first) and commit to the evidence cadence table as an Order Form appendix, we should be able to proceed to signature.

Please confirm acceptance of those two bullets and we'll schedule a short procurement handoff call for Thursday.

Sam
